the Early Miocene magmatic activity of Alaçamdağa volcano-plutonic belt is related to the retreat of the HSCZ, and the crust-mantle interaction during the extensional tectonic processes.

(1) the Alaçamdag granitic and volcanic rock suite is the product of a complex interaction between the sub-continental lithospheric mafic magmatic component and a crustal-derived felsic component during the Early Miocene extensional tectonic processes, (2) the crustal component is more dominant than the mafic magma component, and (3) the crustal-derived component is the result of partial melting of the lower crustal material, (4)

the Early Miocene magmatism of Alaçamdağı was generated by extensional processes, involving the mixing of lower-crust-derived more felsics and enriched subcontinental-lithospheric-mantle-derived more mafics magmas.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Early Miocene magmatic activity of the Alaçemdağ volcano-plutoic complex was generated by the interaction of the subcontinental lithospherics mantle with crustal materials during the early stages of extensional processes.

the Early Miocene extensional processes in north-western Turkey were accompanied by extensive magmatism, the magmatic products having formed by the interaction of mantle-derived magmas and lower crustal materials.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the Early Miocene magmatism was related to the extensional processes in north-western Turkey, and the magmas were generated by mixing of enriched subcontinental lithosphere mantle-derived magmas with lower crustal-derived magmas.

the Early Miocene volcanic and granitic magmatism of the Alaçemdağ complex is the product of a complex interaction between the subduction of the Hellenide oceanic lithosphere, the subsequent collision between the Hellenic arc and the Anatolian continent and the subsequent back-arc extension of the Aegegan basin.
